To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the congruent patterns of ant and plant diversity in Neotropics can be attributed to environmental and spatial factors.
ant and tree species richness are positively associated and that the spatial patterns of ant species richness are strongly correlated with the spatial patterns of tree species richness.

the congruence between ant and tree diversity is weak and that the congruency observed in our study was mainly due to the joint effect of the environmental and the spatial factors on both ant and tree diversity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of cross-taxon congruent patterns of diversity and their implications for conservation planning.
the mechanisms behind the observed cross-taxon congruent patterns of diversity.
understanding the mechanisms behind cross-taxon congruent diversity patterns and their potential to serve as surrogates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
congruence between ant and tree diversity is not universal, but it may be more common than we think.
the observed patterns of ant and plant diversity are congruent in the Cerrado but not necessarily in all savanna regions of the world.
the congruent spatial patterns of ant diversity and tree diversity are a function of the joint effects of the environmental and the spatial factors on both groups of organisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, at least in Neotropical Savannas, the spatial distribution of tree diversity can be a good predictor of ant diversity.
, at least in the Cerrado, ants and trees are not independent of each other.
ant diversity in Neotropican savannas is not strongly related to tree diversity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the mechanisms underlying the congruence in species richness and community structure of different taxa may be complex and difficult to unravel, and that the use of surrogate taxa should be evaluated on a case-by-case basis.
the strength of the plant–animal diversity relationship is likely to be idiosynchratic, and that it depends on the specific biota and the environmental context.
, at a regional scale and in a Neotropical savanna, ant and tree diversity patterns are congruent, and that this congruency arises from the joint influence of environmental and spatial gradients.
